Subject: Staffing Review and Assignment Plan for Multi-Station Service Center

Overview
We are preparing the next staffing plan for our multi-station service center. Each station operates as a distinct help desk, counter, or department with its own customer arrival patterns. A variety of staff types are available, each with different skills, hourly costs, and work rates that vary by station. Some staff types are not qualified to work at certain stations. The key decision is how many people of each staff type to assign to each station to meet service standards at the lowest sustainable hourly cost.

Current Operating Situation
- Demand: We track hourly customer arrivals by station. Demand differs from station to station and must be met locally.
- Workforce: Multiple staff types are available, each with a limited headcount and different hourly costs. Work rates are not uniform; the same staff type may handle customers faster at one station than another.
- Qualifications: Certain staff-station combinations are not permitted due to certification or capability requirements.

Staffing Challenge
The scheduling space includes hundreds of plausible staff-to-station assignments, with a meaningful share ruled out by qualifications. Handling speed for each staff type and station is expressed as an average number of minutes per customer, while arrivals are expressed as customers per hour. To plan effectively, we must interpret these two measures on a comparable basis and determine the right mix of qualified staff types at each station so that service capacity comfortably stays ahead of incoming demand.

Service Quality and Policy Requirements
- Utilization policy: We deliberately avoid running stations at the ragged edge. Staff at a station should not be busy more than a target fraction of their time on average. In practical terms, the combined throughput of the assigned team at each station must exceed the expected incoming volume with a meaningful safety margin, so that queues do not build and staff have breathing room for variability.
- Minimum coverage: Each station must have at least a baseline on-duty presence, regardless of short-term demand, to ensure coverage, safety, and continuity.
- Skills and eligibility: We will only assign staff where they are qualified to serve. Unqualified combinations are treated as unavailable.
- Availability: The number of staff we can schedule of each type is limited by actual availability. We cannot assign more of a given type than we have on hand.

Cost Objective
Staff types carry different hourly labor costs. The goal is to meet all service requirements while minimizing total hourly staffing cost. The plan should select the least-cost combination of qualified staff that:
- Meets or exceeds station-level demand with a buffer consistent with the utilization policy,
- Satisfies minimum coverage at every station,
- Respects staff availability limits by type,
- Uses only qualified assignments.

Approach and Next Steps
- Data alignment: We will use the current arrival rates by station and the handling time matrix (minutes per customer by staff type and station). Because demand is measured per hour and handling is measured in minutes per customer, we will interpret staff handling times as practical throughput when evaluating how many people of each type are needed to keep station load below the utilization target.
- Feasibility screen: We will remove unqualified staff-station pairs from consideration and cap the number of assignable staff of each type at their available headcount.
- Coverage and capacity: For each station, we will ensure the assigned staffing meets minimum coverage and provides enough effective capacity to stay comfortably ahead of incoming customers in line with our utilization policy.
- Cost minimization: Among all feasible assignments that satisfy the above, we will choose the mix that yields the lowest total hourly cost.

Deliverables
- A station-by-station roster indicating the recommended number of staff by type,
- A summary of expected station load relative to the utilization target, demonstrating the buffer at each station,
- A cost roll-up with comparisons to alternative mixes where relevant,
- Sensitivity notes showing how recommendations change with shifts in arrival volume or staff availability.

Decision Request
Upon review of the attached data and proposed plan, we will ask for approval to implement the recommended staffing mix for the next scheduling cycle and to adopt the utilization and minimum coverage targets as ongoing operating policies for this center.

Subject: Staffing Review and Assignment Plan for Multi-Station Service Center

Overview
We are preparing the next staffing plan for our multi-station service center. Each station operates as a distinct help desk, counter, or department with its own customer arrival patterns. A variety of staff types are available, each with different skills, hourly costs, and work rates that vary by station. Some staff types are not qualified to work at certain stations. The key decision is how many people of each staff type to assign to each station to meet service standards at the lowest sustainable hourly cost.

Current Operating Situation
- Demand: We track hourly customer arrivals by station. Demand differs from station to station and must be met locally.
- Workforce: Multiple staff types are available, each with a limited headcount and different hourly costs. Work rates are not uniform; the same staff type may handle customers faster at one station than another.
- Qualifications: Certain staff-station combinations are not permitted due to certification or capability requirements.

Staffing Challenge
The scheduling space includes hundreds of plausible staff-to-station assignments, with a meaningful share ruled out by qualifications. Handling speed for each staff type and station is expressed as an average number of minutes per customer, while arrivals are expressed as customers per hour. To plan effectively, we must interpret these two measures on a comparable basis and determine the right mix of qualified staff types at each station so that service capacity comfortably stays ahead of incoming demand.

Service Quality and Policy Requirements
- Utilization policy: We deliberately avoid running stations at the ragged edge. Staff at a station should not be busy more than a target fraction of their time on average. In practical terms, the combined throughput of the assigned team at each station must exceed the expected incoming volume with a meaningful safety margin, so that queues do not build and staff have breathing room for variability.
- Minimum coverage: Each station must have at least a baseline on-duty presence, regardless of short-term demand, to ensure coverage, safety, and continuity.
- Skills and eligibility: We will only assign staff where they are qualified to serve. Unqualified combinations are treated as unavailable.
- Availability: The number of staff we can schedule of each type is limited by actual availability. We cannot assign more of a given type than we have on hand.

Cost Objective
Staff types carry different hourly labor costs. The goal is to meet all service requirements while minimizing total hourly staffing cost. The plan should select the least-cost combination of qualified staff that:
- Meets or exceeds station-level demand with a buffer consistent with the utilization policy,
- Satisfies minimum coverage at every station,
- Respects staff availability limits by type,
- Uses only qualified assignments.

Approach and Next Steps
- Data alignment: We will use the current arrival rates by station and the handling time matrix (minutes per customer by staff type and station). Because demand is measured per hour and handling is measured in minutes per customer, we will interpret staff handling times as practical throughput when evaluating how many people of each type are needed to keep station load below the utilization target.
- Feasibility screen: We will remove unqualified staff-station pairs from consideration and cap the number of assignable staff of each type at their available headcount.
- Coverage and capacity: For each station, we will ensure the assigned staffing meets minimum coverage and provides enough effective capacity to stay comfortably ahead of incoming customers in line with our utilization policy.
- Cost minimization: Among all feasible assignments that satisfy the above, we will choose the mix that yields the lowest total hourly cost.

Deliverables
- A station-by-station roster indicating the recommended number of staff by type,
- A summary of expected station load relative to the utilization target, demonstrating the buffer at each station,
- A cost roll-up with comparisons to alternative mixes where relevant,
- Sensitivity notes showing how recommendations change with shifts in arrival volume or staff availability.

Decision Request
Upon review of the attached data and proposed plan, we will ask for approval to implement the recommended staffing mix for the next scheduling cycle and to adopt the utilization and minimum coverage targets as ongoing operating policies for this center.
